kicker: From the summit you can see the clouds — but the clouds can also hide the path.
summary: AI news arrives every week — ask who measured it, how, and who checked it again.

quiz.q: A company says its new model “beats every rival”. What is the first question to ask?
options: Who measured it, and with which test?
Does the new model have a nice name?
How many likes did the launch post get?
How much money has the company raised?
quiz.explain: Scores a company measures itself are the company's own claim. Find out who measured, with what, then look for an outside check.

peaks.label: The peaks
peaks.art: You stand on a mossy rock ridge above a valley full of cloud. A big moon has just risen on the right. Five pointed rock peaks rise out of the sea of cloud on an arc, their shadows lying long to the left across it. On each crown sits a low stone slab carved with one model launch, in date order from left to right, joined by a fine broken stroke of ink. From here all five look the same height. A leaning pine stands on the left, a stone lantern on the right.
peaks.hint: Drag to stand somewhere else: the nearer peak looks taller. Touch a peak to turn its stele, touch the stone lantern to show verified news only, press Esc to come back.
peaks.group: Steles for the new models, in order of release date
peaks.verifiedOnlyAria: Show only steles an independent party has confirmed
peaks.othersNote: Grok (xAI), Qwen (Alibaba), Mistral… are big mountain ranges too. AI Zen has not yet checked their latest releases, so no steles stand for them yet.

insight.text: The 2026 summit has many owners. A stele gives name, date and source — never “strongest”, because every test ranks differently.

detail.text: Between 21 July and 28 September 2026 alone: Gemini 3.6 Flash (Google), GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), then Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (Anthropic) launched one after another.

gate.label: The fenced summit
gate.art: Eye level, right against the bamboo fence on the highest summit. A few blurred bamboo stalks at the edges; in the middle a gate of two latticed wooden doors, barred by a wooden bolt. Through the lattice, lamplight inside: a wall laid in lines of code, a red crack, two workers patching it, two stone lanterns, twelve small lamps along the wall and, further off, a faint band of lights. Behind the wall rise the summit, the moon and the mist.
gate.gateAria: Slide the wooden bolt aside to open the gate and see why this model is restricted (or press Enter)

reason.text: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview finds and exploits software flaws so well that it should not be released widely yet, so it goes only to defenders.

gate.courtArt: Looking down on the fenced summit floating in the sea of cloud, like a temple ground plan. A raked gravel court in the middle, four gates at the four quarters. Outside each gate stand a lantern bearer and a carved sign: the gate itself, a stone with fresh mortar, a stone with a single notch, a smaller fenced ring. Open a gate and its bearer walks to the middle of the court, leaving footprints.

view.text: Mythos Preview has found thousands of serious, previously unknown flaws (zero-days) in every major operating system and browser, so they must be patched before any wider release.

stones.who: Mozilla · a tester, maker of the Firefox browser (05/2026)

view.text: Firefox 150 fixed 271 bugs found by Mythos Preview, 180 rated high — a measure of urgency, not proof they were ever exploited.
Glasswing drew huge attention but offered very little hard data: at that point only one public flaw ID (CVE) could be tied directly to the project.
GPT-6 Astra is also opening gradually, first to selected customers, because the company rates its own cybersecurity ability as “Critical”.

common.text: Agreed: AI is already very good at finding flaws. Disputed: who gets access, when, and who checks the companies' claims.

insight.text: The 2026 trend: the strongest models may not reach everyone at once, but open gradually — defenders first.

detail.text: Project Glasswing (7 April 2026): Mythos Preview went to 12 launch partners such as AWS, Apple and the Linux Foundation, plus more than 40 organisations that maintain critical software.

stele.label: Reading the stele without being fooled
stele.art: A large stone stele under a pavilion roof, carved with a mock press release in big letters. The visitor sweeps a paper lantern across it: in the lantern light, five faint carvings appear beside the loudest sentences.
stele.lanternAria: Sweep the lantern over the stele, or use Tab to move through each sentence and press Enter
stele.mockTitle: PRESS RELEASE · Launching the Shooting Star model

mockNote.text: The press release and the “Shooting Star” model are mock-ups written by AI Zen for practising how to read the news.

lines.text: Shooting Star beats EVERY rival on 12 benchmarks!
lines.question: Did the company score itself, or did someone outside? Which benchmark, under what conditions?
lines.aria: Inspect: beats every rival on 12 benchmarks

lines.text: Watch: Shooting Star builds an app in 30 seconds.
lines.question: Is the video the best run out of how many tries? Have you tried it on your own work?
lines.aria: Inspect: video of an app built in 30 seconds

lines.text: Technical details will be published later.
lines.question: Is there a system card or technical report that spells out the limits and risks?
lines.aria: Inspect: technical details will be published later

lines.text: Available to everyone from today*  (*premium plan, usage limits apply)
lines.question: Who can really use it, at what price, and how many times a day?
lines.aria: Inspect: available to everyone from today, with a small asterisk

lines.question: Which experts — are they named? Have researchers, reputable press or real users checked it yet?
lines.aria: Inspect: experts rate it very highly

stele.done: All five signs — open the takeaway card

insight.text: AI news earns trust when it answers: who measured, how, what it costs, its limits, and who outside checked it.

detail.text: Even on the Claude Opus 5.5 launch page, Anthropic wrote that in its own use the gap between Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 is narrower than the scores suggest. Benchmarks don't tell the whole story.

tide.label: The release tide
tide.art: Lying at the water’s edge at one end of a long tidal flat that runs diagonally into the distance, to a mountain with cloud round its summit: time runs into depth. The tide is in, water covers the flat and the moon’s broken road runs toward you. Drag the moon across the sky and the water draws back toward the mountain while the stones rise in date order: far apart near you, crowding at the mountain’s foot and climbing its flank like steps.
tide.prompt: Drag the moon through the years
tide.moonAria: Drag the moon, or use the ← → keys to move through the milestones
tide.paceNote: No reliable source counts releases per quarter, so the scroll uses Epoch AI's count of large-scale models instead.

fact.text: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT, letting anyone chat with a large language model.
According to Epoch AI, GPT-4 was the first model trained with more than 10²⁵ operations (FLOP).
Throughout 2024, about two models at that scale were announced each month on average.
By June 2025, Epoch AI counted more than 30 models at GPT-4 scale or above, from 12 developers.
Anthropic announces Claude Mythos Preview but does not release it widely, giving it only to organisations that find and fix security flaws.
Between 21 July and 28 September 2026, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic released four new models — in under ten weeks.

horizon.text: The pace of releases may keep quickening — but that is a guess; no one can see through the clouds on the summit yet.

insight.text: In 2023 there was one model at GPT-4 scale; by mid-2025 there were over 30. New peaks rise faster than we can read the news.

tide.detail: Training scale doesn't say how capable a model is, but it shows more and more companies can climb the mountain — and “beats every rival” headlines will keep coming thick and fast.

mozilla-mythos.note: Mozilla is a user, not the model's maker. Firefox 150 fixed 271 bugs found by Mythos Preview: 180 high, 80 moderate, 11 low. Mozilla notes the ratings measure urgency, not proof of exploitation.

cso-glasswing.note: Cites VulnCheck's analysis (Patrick Garrity). Written before Mozilla's report of 7 May 2026.

bleeping-gpt6.note: Quotes OpenAI's system card: GPT-6 Astra reaches the “Critical” cybersecurity threshold under the company's own framework. OpenAI's original page blocks lookup tools, so it has not been opened directly.
